economics.economic-problem-explain.0020.all: Reduces quantity of labour (working-age, young workers) -> fewer workers, skills shortages, lower productive capacity / PPF shifts inward; possibly less enterprise too.

economics.economic-problem-mcq-auth.0006.all: the game of football given up

economics.economic-problem-mcq-def.0001.all: Resources limited while wants unlimited, so choices must be made

economics.economic-problem-state.0008.all: What to produce (or how to produce / for whom to produce)

economics.economic-problem-state-class.0.all: An entrepreneur taking the risk of opening a new shop / organising the other factors

economics.exchange-data.0014.b: Uncertain export revenue/import costs in rand; hard to set prices and plan investment; profit margins squeezed; may need hedging costs; reduces investment and trade; link to 9% monthly change.
economics.exchange-data.0014.c: For: stability aids planning, investment, exports, inflation control. Against: costly use of reserves, interest rate changes harm growth, may fail against market forces, loses monetary independence. Depends on cause and reserves.

economics.globalisation-analyse-3.0004.all: Low wages/poor conditions, exploitation; profits repatriated; reliance on MNCs which may relocate (footloose) causing unemployment; dependence on low-value manufacturing; environmental costs. NB context implausible for Singapore (high-wage economy).

economics.globalisation-mcq-def.0001.all: The growing integration and interdependence of the world's economies...

economics.globalisation-state.0001.all: Access to cheaper labour / new markets / avoid tariffs

economics.globalisation-state-class.0002.all: Profits sent back to the home country

economics.government-analyse-1.0008.all: Job losses as private owner cuts costs to raise profit; wage/condition changes; possible higher pay/training via investment as passenger numbers rise; union conflict/strikes; loss of job security.

economics.government-analyse-2.0007.all: Lower fares (prices rising faster than inflation) as not profit-driven; improved service via government investment; integrated network; protect jobs; social objectives over profit.

economics.government-assess-1.0004.all: Benefit: efficiency, investment, competition, better service given rising demand. Against: private monopoly raises prices, safety cuts without subsidies. Depends on regulation and competition.

economics.government-assess-2.0002.all: For: prices rising, poor service, natural monopoly, essential good. Against: cost to taxpayer, government inefficiency, lack of profit incentive; alternative stronger regulation.

economics.government-define1.0004.all: Removal of rules/regulations restricting firms, to increase competition

economics.government-define2.0002.all: Transfer of a firm/industry from private sector into public sector (state) ownership

economics.government-describe.0013.all: Raises revenue from the sale, which can fund spending or reduce borrowing; also removes need for subsidies

economics.government-evaluate-1.0007.all: As assess-1 with judgement: depends on regulator, competition from other airports, use of rising passenger revenue; short vs long run.

economics.government-evaluate-2.0007.all: For: prices, service, natural monopoly/essential. Against: cost, inefficiency; alternatives regulation/price caps. Judgement depends on cause of poor service.

economics.government-explain.0011.all: To protect 18,000 jobs; avoiding unemployment and multiplier effects on local economy and lost tax revenue/benefit costs; also strategic energy supply.

economics.government-mcq-class.0001.all: The government selling its national airline to private investors

economics.government-mcq-def.0001.all: Transfer from public sector to private sector

economics.growth-analyse-1.0003.all: Higher incomes/living standards, more jobs, higher tax revenue for public services, firm profits and investment; benefits from new factories and mines.

economics.growth-analyse-2.0001.all: Falling demand/sales and revenue, lower profits, reduced investment, redundancies, possible closures; high energy costs raise costs; inferior-good firms may gain.

economics.globalisation-analyse-3.0004.problem: Context is factually implausible: Singapore is a high-wage economy and does not have over 1 million low-wage garment workers (about a quarter of its workforce).
economics.globalisation-analyse-3.0004.fix: Use a low-wage garment-exporting country (e.g. Bangladesh or Cambodia) or a fictional country name.

economics.globalisation-state-class.0002.problem: Grammatical error in stem: 'State one a drawback'.
economics.globalisation-state-class.0002.fix: State one drawback for a host country when multinational corporations set up there.
